title: Latency-headroom allocator: phase coalescing and responsive fairness policy
creator: Nadia Ortega
description:
Problem: High-precedence short-latency requests are intermittently suffering p95 tail spikes during competing long-prefill workloads. Current token-phase splitters can either favor latency (sacrificing throughput) or favor throughput (causing latency spikes). There is no runtime feedback loop accounting for measured latency headroom to opportunistically coalesce adjacent micro-phases without starving latency-sensitive flows.

Proposal: Implement a Latency-Headroom Allocator (LHA) that: 1) continuously measures per-queue latency headroom (difference between SLO target and observed p95/p99), 2) uses that headroom to safely coalesce adjacent micro-phases (phase coalescing) when headroom is positive, and 3) enforces a responsive fairness policy that reclaims coalesced capacity as headroom decreases. The allocator will emit kernel-selection hints so the runtime can pick specialized attention kernels when coalescing changes memory/attn patterns.

Key design points and tradeoffs: - Conservative coalescing window: prefer small coalesces (1-2 micro-slices) and only when headroom margin >= 15ms to bound added latency. Tradeoff: smaller wins lower throughput gains but reduce regressions. - Fairness reclaim: implement soft tokens per-customer; reclaimed capacity uses hedged fallback so reclaiming doesn't cause sudden stalls. - Kernel hints: coalescing will annotate requests with an affinity tag (e.g., ATTEN_SPARSE_HINT) to prefer kernels optimized for denser attention states; this is a best-effort signal, not gating allocation. - Safety net: every allocation must keep a reserved fast-path token pool sized to 5% of GPU cycles or min(2 concurrent slots) to preserve tail SLO for small requests.

Metrics and targets: - Latency: no more than +2% p95 for latency-sensitive routes (target unchanged), aim for 10-20% p95 improvement on mixed workloads. - Throughput: 8-20% throughput uplift on batchy long-prefill workloads in synthetic tests. - Fairness: no individual tenant should see >10% increased wait time vs baseline for steady-state traffic.

Testing and rollout: 1) Local benchmark harness (unit microbenchmarks) -> 2) Integration test in perf staging with traffic replay from production traces -> 3) Canary 5% traffic (low-risk customers) with automatic rollback on latency/regression triggers -> 4) Gradual ramp to 50% then 100%.

Observability: add per-route headroom metric, coalesce_count, coalesce_size_histogram, kernel_hint_recommendations, and per-tenant reclaim_events. Wire these into console-runtime dashboards and add alerts when headroom drops below safety threshold.

Docs and links: design doc (internal), benchmark dashboards, and prototype PR linked in attachments.

Risks and mitigations: - Over-aggressive coalescing could regress tail latency: mitigated by conservative thresholds and an emergency reclaim circuit. - Kernel hint mismatch: hints are advisory; ensure runtimes fall back gracefully. - Multi-tenant fairness complexity: start with per-queue fairness and iterate based on telemetry.
